images.title: Gas lines during the 1979 energy crisis
images.description: The gas lines: the era's defining image of stagflation.

images.title: Freed American hostages from Iran arriving home in January 1981
images.description: The hostages came home the same day Reagan took the oath, January 20, 1981.

images.title: Portrait of economist Arthur Laffer
images.description: Laffer argued cutting tax rates could bring in more government revenue.

images.title: Diagram of the Laffer curve
images.description: The curve that fit supply-side theory on a napkin.

images.title: George H. W. Bush campaigning in the 1980 Republican primaries
images.description: Reagan's rival called supply-side 'voodoo economics' during the 1980 primaries before joining the ticket.

images.title: Ronald Reagan at a 1980 campaign rally
images.description: Reagan sold the same theory as 'supply-side' economics on the 1980 campaign trail.

images.title: Reagan signing the 1981 tax cut into law
images.description: The 1981 law cut income tax rates about a quarter over three years; the top rate fell from 70 to 50 percent.

images.title: The United States Capitol
images.description: Congress bought the supply-side theory and passed the 1981 tax law.

images.title: The Pentagon
images.description: Reagan handed the military a much bigger budget while cutting taxes, the other half of the deficit squeeze.

images.title: A B-1 strategic bomber
images.description: The military buildup of the 1980s poured money into weapons systems like the B-1.

images.title: Chart of the U.S. national debt climbing through the 1980s
images.description: The debt went from about $900 billion in 1980 to over $2 trillion by 1986.

images.title: An AT&T Long Lines facility
images.description: AT&T's long-distance monopoly was broken up in the Reagan deregulation wave.

images.title: CNN, the first 24-hour cable news channel
images.description: Cable television was deregulated as Washington loosened rules on business.

images.title: Reagan announcing the firing of the striking air traffic controllers, August 1981
images.description: In August 1981 Reagan fired every striking PATCO controller, telling organized labor the old rules were gone.

images.title: An airport control tower in the 1980s
images.description: The towers that coordinated the fired controllers' airspace.

images.title: The New York Stock Exchange trading floor in the 1980s
images.description: The tax cuts helped people who paid a lot of income tax, which meant the wealthy.

images.title: Wall Street in the 1980s
images.description: The money people of the conservative coalition wanted lower taxes and deregulation.

images.title: Cabrini-Green public housing in Chicago
images.description: The poor pay little income tax, so rate cuts meant nothing while housing aid was cut.

images.title: Reagan taking questions at a White House press conference
images.description: The administration promised the cuts would pay for themselves.

images.title: Reagan delivering his first inaugural address, January 20, 1981
images.description: 'Government is not the solution to our problem, government is the problem' became the era's signature line.

images.title: Barry Goldwater campaigning for president in 1964
images.description: Goldwater's landslide loss planted the seed of the conservative coalition on small government and states' rights.

images.title: The 1964 Republican National Convention
images.description: The convention that nominated Goldwater proved the conservative audience existed.

images.title: Portrait of preacher Jerry Falwell
images.description: In 1979 Falwell founded the Moral Majority, mobilizing evangelical Christians into a political force.

images.title: Jerry Falwell and the Moral Majority
images.description: In 1979 Falwell founded the Moral Majority, mobilizing evangelicals into a political force.

images.title: The Heritage Foundation headquarters in Washington
images.description: Founded in 1973, Heritage supplied ready-made conservative policy for the Reagan White House.

images.title: An auto assembly line in the 1980s
images.description: Reagan Democrats were often union members in the industrial Midwest.

images.title: A labor union meeting in the 1980s
images.description: Working-class union voters crossed over to Reagan in 1980 and 1984.

images.title: The Neshoba County Fairgrounds in Mississippi
images.description: Reagan's August 1980 'states' rights' speech at the fairgrounds.

images.title: Memorial to the civil rights workers murdered in Neshoba County in 1964
images.description: The fairgrounds sit near where three civil rights workers were murdered in 1964.

images.title: Reagan speaking at the Neshoba County Fair in 1980
images.description: Historians argue whether 'states' rights' there was a coded racial signal or standard federalism.

images.title: The Mississippi State Capitol
images.description: 'States' rights' was the old language of resistance to integration, which is why critics heard a signal.

images.title: The Chicago skyline in the 1970s
images.description: Reagan's 'welfare queen' stories were set in Chicago, starting on the 1976 campaign trail.

images.title: Reagan campaigning in 1976
images.description: The welfare-queen anecdote, with its inflated numbers, dated to Reagan's 1976 run.

images.title: Reagan delivering the 'evil empire' speech in 1983
images.description: In 1983 Reagan called the Soviet Union an 'evil empire,' the posture beat of this lesson's Cold War coda.

images.title: Reagan speaking at the Berlin Wall in June 1987
images.description: 'Tear down this wall': the clip everyone knows, parked here for next lesson's story.

images.title: The Berlin Wall in the mid-1980s
images.description: The Wall as it stood when Reagan gave the 1987 speech, distinct from the speech photo.

images.title: Portrait of Walter Mondale
images.description: Carter's vice president ran in 1984 attacking supply-side and promising to raise taxes.

images.title: Geraldine Ferraro campaigning in 1984
images.description: The first woman on a major party's national ticket, Mondale's running mate.

images.title: Reagan campaigning for reelection in 1984
images.description: 'Morning again in America' carried Reagan to 49 states.

images.title: Electoral map of the 1984 presidential election
images.description: Reagan took everything but Minnesota and D.C. in the 1984 landslide.

images.title: Reagan meeting with his cabinet in 1981
images.description: The verdict's paradox: conservatism became the default setting, but government was redirected, not shrunk.

images.title: A U.S. aircraft carrier in the 1980s
images.description: The military grew while the deficit grew: the government got redirected.

images.title: Panels of the AIDS Memorial Quilt on the National Mall
images.description: The AIDS crisis began in 1981; the administration's slow response became its own indictment.

images.title: Homelessness in America in the 1980s
images.description: Homelessness rose in the cities while social services were cut.

images.title: Downtown Phoenix
images.description: The Sunbelt, booming and leaning conservative, was the coalition map strand.

images.title: Reagan signing the Tax Reform Act of 1986
images.description: The 1986 law dropped the top rate to 28 percent; the debt doubled anyway.

images.title: The 1980 Republican National Convention in Detroit
images.description: The convention that united the coalition's strands behind the Reagan ticket.

images.title: Ronald Reagan's official presidential portrait
images.description: The verdict: he didn't shrink the government, he changed what it was for.

images.title: A postwar American suburb
images.description: 'Morning again in America' sold suburban prosperity as the payoff of Reaganomics.

images.title: The federal deficit under Reaganomics
images.description: Cut the income, raise the outgo: the deficit had nowhere to go but up.

images.title: A savings and loan in the 1980s
images.description: Banking was one of the industries deregulated under Reagan.

images.title: A payphone in the 1980s
images.description: Long-distance phone service was deregulated in the Reagan years.

images.title: An American classroom in the 1980s
images.description: Education money got cut while the wealthy kept the gains of the rate cuts.

images.title: An MX Peacekeeper missile
images.description: New missiles like the MX soaked up the bigger 1980s military budget.

images.title: Grocery prices in the 1970s
images.description: Stagflation's daily face: prices climbing while the economy stalled.

images.title: The White House
images.description: The new administration took office as the hostages came home.

images.title: A megachurch congregation
images.description: Falwell's Moral Majority turned churchgoers into a mobilized political force.

images.title: A steel mill in the 1980s
images.description: The industrial Midwest and Northeast: home of the Reagan Democrats.

images.title: The welfare system of the 1970s
images.description: The real Chicago woman was convicted in 1977 of fraud worth about eight thousand dollars.

images.title: The Reagan-Bush ticket in 1980
images.description: Voodoo economics' critic became the running mate.

images.title: A Strategic Defense Initiative test in the 1980s
images.description: SDI, the missile shield critics nicknamed Star Wars.

images.title: Detroit in the 1980s
images.description: The industrial Midwest: home of the Reagan Democrats.

images.title: Reagan in the Oval Office, 1981
images.description: Ready-made policy let the Reagan White House govern from day one.
